title: Wheel and Tire Safety Precautions
introduction:
I check tire-sealant history and service-equipment compatibility before wheel work begins. Sealant can create a fire or explosion hazard, while the wrong machine can damage a wheel even when it looks capable of doing the job. A wheel face is a finished surface, not a convenient place for a machine to grab.

This guide covers the required equipment characteristics, wheel-finish protection and tire-care principles. It is not a tire-changing, balancing or alignment procedure. Use the vehicle's applicable inflation and rotation information alongside it; pressure values and rotation intervals are not specified here.

items.name: Establish sealant history
items.detail: Ask the customer whether anyone has injected tire sealant into the tire before servicing it. Sealant may be flammable and can burn or explode when exposed to an ignition source, with a risk of serious personal injury.

requirements.category: Equipment for carbon fiber and alloy wheels

items.name: Confirm machine contact points
items.detail: Use a center-clamp tire changer, a balancer that does not contact the wheel face and a non-spade alignment machine that does not grip or contact the wheel's outside edge. The equipment examples and damage consequences are detailed below.

items.name: Prepare tools suited to the weight style
items.detail: Have designated wheel-weight removal pliers for clip-on weights, and designated adhesive-weight removal pliers or a non-metal adhesive-weight scraper for adhesive weights. Denatured alcohol may assist with adhesive residue if needed.

edits.text: WARNING: Before servicing any tire, ask the customer whether anyone has injected tire sealant into it. Tire sealants may be flammable and can burn or explode if exposed to an ignition source. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Sealant history is a required preparation check because material inside the tire can change the service hazard.

edits.text: NOTICE: Use the wheel-compatible service equipment described below.
edits.why: The following equipment restrictions protect the wheels from service damage.

edits.text: Ford Equipment Guidance for Carbon Fiber and Alloy Wheels
edits.why: Although the original heading presents recommendations, the individual equipment instructions explicitly state Ford's requirements.

edits.text: Ford requires a center clamp style tire changer, such as Hunter® Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or an equivalent. Other designs, especially tabletop machines, are highly likely to cause wheel damage that is not warrantable. Do not use tabletop machines that grip the inside of the wheel and ride on the front wheel flange to remove the tire; wheel damage will occur.
edits.why: I check how the machine holds the wheel, rather than judging compatibility by whether the tire fits on it.

edits.text: Ford requires a wheel balancer that does not contact the wheel face, such as Hunter® Road Force Touch GSP9700. Do not use a machine that contacts the wheel face; wheel damage will occur.
edits.why: The decisive feature is keeping the machine's contact away from the wheel face.

edits.text: Ford requires a non-spade style alignment machine, such as Hunter® Hawkeye Elite or an equivalent. Other designs are highly likely to cause wheel damage that is not warrantable. Do not use machines that grip or contact the outside edge of the wheel; wheel damage will occur.
edits.why: The attachment method matters even though alignment does not involve removing the tire.

edits.text: NOTICE: Do not clean aluminum wheels with steel wool, abrasive-type cleaners or strong detergents. These can damage the wheel finish.
edits.why: Cleaning must preserve the finished surface rather than abrade or chemically damage it.

edits.text: NOTICE: Use only industry-standard tools to remove wheel balance weights. Remove clip-on weights with designated wheel-weight removal pliers. For adhesive weights, use designated adhesive-weight removal pliers or a non-metal adhesive-weight scraper. Never use a screwdriver or another sharp metallic instrument to remove adhesive weights. If needed, use denatured alcohol to help remove adhesive residue. Ignoring these guidelines can damage the wheel finish.
edits.why: Match the tool to the weight's attachment method so removal does not turn into scraping the finished wheel surface.

edits.text: Factory-installed tires and wheels are designed to operate satisfactorily with loads up to and including the full-rated load capacity when inflated to the recommended pressures.
edits.why: The load-capacity statement depends on correct inflation; capacity and pressure must be considered together.

edits.text: Correct tire pressure and driving technique strongly influence tire life. Heavy cornering, excessively rapid acceleration and unnecessary sharp braking increase tire wear.
edits.why: Tire wear reflects how the tire is inflated and used, not simply how long it has been fitted.

edits.text: Rotate the tires at the recommended intervals to help equalize wear.
edits.why: Rotation shares wear among positions; the applicable rotation information supplies the interval and arrangement.
